literal: Attendant Wei Sengqie understood wind augury and memorialized that an act of violent treason was about to occur at once.
idiomatic: Attendant Wei Sengqie, skilled in wind augury, reported that treason was imminent.

literal: The emperor pretended there was an emergency in Ye, strung his bow and wrapped his spear-shaft, galloped into the southern city, ordered Deng Changyang to confine the Empress Dowager in the Northern Palace, and issued an edict that none of the inner or outer kin might see the Empress Dowager on any account.
idiomatic: The emperor feigned an emergency in Ye, strung his bow and wrapped his spear, galloped into the southern city, and ordered Deng Changyang to confine the Empress Dowager in the Northern Palace, with an edict forbidding all kin, near or distant, from seeing her.

literal: After some time, the emperor welcomed the Empress Dowager back.
idiomatic: After some time the emperor welcomed the Empress Dowager back.

literal: When the Empress Dowager first heard that an envoy had arrived, she was greatly alarmed, fearing something unforeseen.
idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager first heard that an envoy had come, she was terrified, fearing the worst.

literal: Whenever the Empress Dowager set out food, the emperor would not dare to taste it.
idiomatic: Whenever the Empress Dowager set out a meal, the emperor dared not taste it.

literal: An envoy from Zhou, Yuan Wei, came on a diplomatic mission and composed the "Rhapsody on a Journey," recounting Duke Zhuang of Zheng's suppression of Duan and removal of Lady Jiang; though the writing was not polished, people at the time felt deeply shamed by it.
idiomatic: Yuan Wei, an envoy from Zhou, came on a diplomatic visit and composed the "Rhapsody on a Journey," recounting how Duke Zhuang of Zheng crushed his brother Duan and banished their mother Lady Jiang; though the prose was crude, the court felt deeply shamed.

literal: When Qi fell, she entered Zhou and gave free rein to lewd conduct.
idiomatic: When Qi fell she entered Zhou and gave herself over to debauchery.

literal: She died during the Kaihuang era of Sui.
idiomatic: She died during the Kaihuang era of Sui.

literal: Houzhu, Empress Hulu
idiomatic: Houzhu, Empress Hulu

literal: Empress Hulu of Houzhu, née Hulu, was the daughter of Left Chancellor Hulu Guang.
idiomatic: Empress Hulu of Houzhu, née Hulu, was the daughter of Left Chancellor Hulu Guang.

literal: At first she was the crown prince's consort.
idiomatic: At first she was the crown prince's consort.

literal: When Houzhu accepted the abdication, she was installed as empress.
idiomatic: When Houzhu accepted the abdication, she was installed as empress.

literal: In the first month of the third year of Wuping she gave birth to a girl; the emperor, wishing to please Guang, falsely claimed a boy had been born and proclaimed a general amnesty.
idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of the Wuping era she bore a girl; the emperor, wishing to please Guang, falsely announced a boy and proclaimed a general amnesty.

literal: When Guang was executed, the empress was deposed and kept in a separate palace; afterward she was ordered to become a nun.
idiomatic: When Guang was executed the empress was deposed to a separate palace, and afterward was ordered to take the tonsure.

literal: When Qi was destroyed, she remarried as the wife of Kaifu Yuan Ren.
idiomatic: When Qi fell she remarried as the wife of Kaifu Yuan Ren.

literal: Houzhu, Empress Hu
idiomatic: Houzhu, Empress Hu

literal: Empress Hu of Houzhu was the daughter of Prince Longdong Changren.
idiomatic: Empress Hu of Houzhu was the daughter of Prince Longdong Changren.

literal: The Empress Dowager Hu, having failed in the way of a mother to the realm, felt deep shame and wished to please Houzhu; she therefore dressed the empress in the palace and had the emperor see her.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu, ashamed at having failed as mother to the realm, wished to please Houzhu; she had the girl dressed and presented in the palace for the emperor to see.

literal: The emperor was indeed pleased, established her as Lady of Hongde, promoted her to Senior Lady of Brilliant Beauty, and greatly favored her.
idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, made her Lady of Hongde, promoted her to senior lady of brilliant beauty, and greatly favored her.

literal: When Empress Hulu was deposed, Lu Aun wished to replace her with Lady Mu, but the Empress Dowager would not allow it.
idiomatic: When Empress Hulu was deposed, Lu Aun wished to install Lady Mu in her place, but the Empress Dowager refused.

literal: Zu Xiaozheng petitioned to install Lady Hu of Brilliant Beauty as empress, and she was thereupon elevated to empress.
idiomatic: Zu Xiaozheng petitioned to make Lady Hu empress, and she was thereupon elevated.

literal: Lu Aun, who had not supported her elevation and had her heart set on Lady Mu, later appeared displeased before the Empress Dowager and said, "What sort of mere niece by blood speaks words like these!
idiomatic: Lu Aun, who had not supported the elevation and still favored Lady Mu, later appeared before the Empress Dowager with a dark look and said, "What sort of niece is this, to speak such words!

literal: The Empress Dowager asked what had been said. She replied, "It cannot be spoken.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager asked what had been said. Lu replied, "It cannot be spoken.

literal: Pressed to answer, she finally said, "She told His Majesty that the Empress Dowager's conduct is largely unlawful and cannot serve as an example.
idiomatic: Pressed again, she finally said, "She told His Majesty that the Empress Dowager's conduct is mostly unlawful and cannot serve as an example.

literal: The Empress Dowager flew into a rage, summoned the empress forth, had her hair shorn on the spot, and sent her back to her family home.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager flew into a rage, summoned the empress, had her head shaved on the spot, and sent her home.

literal: The emperor missed her and repeatedly sent gifts to convey his feelings.
idiomatic: The emperor missed her and repeatedly sent gifts to convey his regard.

literal: Later both she and the deposed Empress Hulu were summoned back within the palace; within days Ye could no longer be held.
idiomatic: Later both she and the deposed Empress Hulu were summoned back into the palace; within days Ye fell.

literal: She too remarried afterward.
idiomatic: She too remarried afterward.

literal: Houzhu, Empress Mu
idiomatic: Houzhu, Empress Mu

literal: Empress Mu of Houzhu, named Yeli, had originally been an attendant of Empress Hulu's household.
idiomatic: Empress Mu of Houzhu, named Yeli, had originally been an attendant in Empress Hulu's household.

literal: Her mother Qingxiao had been a maid to Muzilun, then entered the household of Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Qindao, where an illicit affair produced the future empress; her lineage was unknown, though some said the empress was Song Qindao's own daughter.
idiomatic: Her mother Qingxiao had been a maid to Muzilun, then entered the household of Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Qindao, where an illicit affair produced the future empress; her lineage was unknown, though some said she was Song Qindao's own daughter.

literal: She was called Huanghua as a pet name and later styled Sheli.
idiomatic: Her pet name was Huanghua; later she was styled Sheli.

literal: Song Qindao's wife, jealous, branded Qingxiao's face with the character "Song."
idiomatic: Song Qindao's wife, in jealousy, branded Qingxiao's face with the character for Song.

literal: After Song was executed, Huanghua entered the palace through that connection, won the Last Emperor's favor, and was known within the inner quarters as Director Sheli.
idiomatic: After Song was executed, Huanghua entered the palace by that connection, won Houzhu's favor, and was known within the inner quarters as Director Sheli.

literal: Lady Attendant Lu Taiji, aware of her favor, adopted her as a daughter and recommended her as Lady of Hongde.
idiomatic: Lady Attendant Lu Taiji, knowing of her favor, adopted her as a daughter and recommended her as Lady of Hongde.

literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Wuping she gave birth to the prince Heng.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of the Wuping era she bore Prince Heng.

literal: The emperor still had no heir; Lu maneuvered privately, arguing that the role of regent for the heir could not remain vacant—the reigning empress, Guang's daughter, might resent this—so she had the child raised by the empress and established as crown prince.
idiomatic: The emperor still had no heir; Lu maneuvered in secret, arguing that the regency could not stand empty—the reigning empress, Guang's daughter, might resent it—so she had the child raised by the empress and established as crown prince.

literal: Lu cited the weight of the dynastic surname: Mu paired with Lu, and petitioned that she be granted the surname Mu.
idiomatic: Lu cited the weight of the dynastic surname—Mu paired with Lu—and petitioned that she be granted the surname Mu.

literal: When the deposed Lady Hu was removed, Lu had helped; Hu was then raised to empress and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
idiomatic: When Lady Hu was deposed, Lu had helped; Hu was then raised to empress and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: Earlier, Breakthrough General Yuan Zhenglie had retrieved a seal from the waters east of Ye bearing the inscription "Seal of the Heaven-King's Consort"—a Shi-clan artifact.
idiomatic: Earlier, Breakthrough General Yuan Zhenglie had retrieved a seal from the waters east of Ye inscribed "Seal of the Heaven-King's Consort"—said to be a relic of the Shi clan.

literal: An edict proclaimed this far and wide as an auspicious portent for Empress Mu.
idiomatic: An edict proclaimed the find far and wide as an auspicious portent for Empress Mu.

literal: Under Wucheng a pearl-embroidered skirt and trousers had been made for Empress Hu at immeasurable cost; fire consumed them.
idiomatic: Under Wucheng a pearl-embroidered skirt and trousers had been made for Empress Hu at immeasurable cost, only to be consumed by fire.

literal: After Houzhu installed Empress Mu, such garments were commissioned again.
idiomatic: After Houzhu installed Empress Mu, such garments were commissioned again.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was mourning his mother, envoys Xue Gu and Kang Mai were sent as condolence missions; merchant envoys carried thirty thousand bolts of brocade to buy pearls for a seven-treasure carriage for the empress—the Zhou people refused trade, yet the carriage was built anyway.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was in mourning for his mother, envoys Xue Gu and Kang Mai were sent as condolence missions; merchant envoys carried thirty thousand bolts of brocade to buy pearls for a seven-treasure carriage for the empress—the Zhou people refused to trade, yet the carriage was built anyway.

literal: A children's rhyme had run: "Yellow blossom's vigor will fade; brim the clear cup and pour."
idiomatic: A children's rhyme had run: "Yellow blossom's vigor will fade; brim the clear cup and pour."

literal: It meant Huanghua would not last long; after Houzhu made Mu empress, he drank without measure—hence "brim the clear cup and pour."
idiomatic: It meant Huanghua would not endure; after Houzhu made Mu empress, he drank without measure—hence "brim the clear cup and pour."

literal: Lu ordered Mu Tipo by edict to change his surname to Mu, Lu.
idiomatic: Lu ordered Mu Tipo by edict to take the surnames Mu and Lu.

literal: Taiji—all on account of the empress.
idiomatic: Taiji too—all on account of the empress.

literal: Having taken Lu as her mother and Tipo as her family, the empress no longer acknowledged Qingxiao.
idiomatic: Having taken Lu as her mother and Tipo as her kin, the empress no longer acknowledged Qingxiao.

literal: Qingxiao later healed her face and sought to see her daughter; the Empress Dowager and Lu Aun had her imprisoned and she never gained an audience.
idiomatic: Qingxiao later healed her face and sought to see her daughter; the Empress Dowager and Lu Aun had her imprisoned, and she never gained an audience.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972, as the base for collation.
idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
